cold_email.subject: Interest in Full-Time Educator / Grove City Premium Outlets Pop up — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear lululemon Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Full-Time Educator / Grove City Premium Outlets Pop up opportunity with lululemon at lululemon.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Clinical Research Associate - Sponsor Dedicated — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear IQVIA Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Clinical Research Associate - Sponsor Dedicated opportunity with IQVIA at IQVIA.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in School Secretary (#152312) Buhach Colony High School — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear East Side Union High School District Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the School Secretary (#152312) Buhach Colony High School opportunity with East Side Union High School District at East Side Union High School District.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Circuit Clinical Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Coordinator opportunity with Circuit Clinical at Circuit Clinical.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in 2026-27 AY Lecturer Pool - Biological Sciences — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear California State University-Sacramento Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the 2026-27 AY Lecturer Pool - Biological Sciences opportunity with California State University-Sacramento at California State University-Sacramento.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Patient Service Representative I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Patient Service Representative I opportunity with Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago at Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Clinical Research Assistant — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Adams Clinical Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Clinical Research Assistant opportunity with Adams Clinical at Adams Clinical.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Program Specialist — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear St. Jude Children's Research Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Program Specialist opportunity with St. Jude Children's Research Hospital at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Technician- Chowdhury Lab — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Technician- Chowdhury Lab opportunity with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Clinical Laboratory Scientist I - 2nd Shift — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Abbott Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Clinical Laboratory Scientist I - 2nd Shift opportunity with Abbott at Abbott.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Software Test Engineer 2
jobs.description: What if the work you did every day could impact the lives of people you know? Or all of humanity? At Illumina, we are expanding access to genomic technology to realize health equity for billions of people around the world. Our efforts enable life-changing discoveries that are transforming human health through the early detection and diagnosis of diseases and new treatment options for patients. Working at Illumina means being part of something bigger than yourself. Every person, in every role, has the opportunity to make a difference. Surrounded by extraordinary people, inspiring leaders, and world changing projects, you will do more and become more than you ever thought possible. We are seeking an experienced Software Test Engineer II to support the instrument manufacturing and NPI (new product introduction) development of software for Illumina’s sequencing instruments. This role combines hands-on system testing, technical problem-solving, and close collaboration with cross-functional teams to help ensure the quality and reliability of our next-generation sequencing platforms. The ideal candidate thrives in a multidisciplinary environment and brings curiosity, sound technical judgment, and a quality-first mindset to their work. This is primarily a manufacturing floor support engineer as well as a hands-on, system-level software testing role involving physical sequencing instruments , on-market & future NPI . The role emphasizes test design, exploratory testing, execution, troubleshooting , communicating and collaborating . Coding and test automation skills are valuable but are not the primary focus of the position. Responsibilities: Manufacturing floor support and troubleshoot software , server, cybersecurity, and system- level issues in production and NPI prototype development, evaluating manufacturing Non Conformances Create and implement ECO changes to product and manufacturing processes and system configurations Lead projects to resolve trending issues in manufacturing and the field Work with cross functional teams (Quality, Manufacturing, Development, Regulatory, Supply Chain) to achieve Instrument Manufacturing Operation Goals while maintaining Compliance and security requirements Develop test strategies, plans, and test cases from product, system, and software requirements. Execute functional , integration, system, and regression tests for software features , server applications , and integrations on DNA sequencing instruments. Perform exploratory testing to identify defects, unexpected behaviors, usability concerns, and system-level risks. Own software verification activities for assigned features or subsystems, including planning, execution, defect reporting, and results documentation. Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders to ensure software solutions meet user and system needs. Investigate defects and perform root-cause analysis in collaboration with software, firmware, hardware, manufacturing, and systems teams. Work within established software development, quality, and requirements management processes for regulated products. Participate in requirements, design, and planning activities to identify risks, improve testability, and strengthen verification strategy. Use approved AI-assisted tools to improve test design, exploratory testing, failure analysis, documentation, and workflow efficiency while applying appropriate human review and complying with data privacy, security, and regulated-product quality requirements. The responsibilities listed above are essential but not exhaustive. Individual responsibilities may change based on business needs. Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science , Software Engineering, or a related technical field. 3+ years of professional experience working in software test , software quality, software systems integration, or a related role. Experience with functional , integration, system, and regression testing. Experience independently owning feature-level or subsystem-level software verification activities. Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills, including the ability to isolate failures across software, firmware, hardware, and system boundaries. Familiarity with defect tracking and requirements management platforms such as Jira and Jama. Ability to work regularly with physical instruments in a laboratory environment. Familiarity with Linux and Windows OS environments and command-line tools. Familiarity with data management and processing via server, single-board compute or compute engines Familiarity with production and customer network/IT setup & different configurations that may impact installation or manufacturing processes Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a willingness to learn from and share knowledge with others. Nice to Have: Familiarity with embedded systems, communication protocols, or integrating software with hardware modules. Has experience developing/executing simple and complex test automation protocols Cybersecurity regulation knowledge and best practices Familiarity working in a regulated environment, such as medical devices. Experience using AI-assisted engineering tools to support software testing, troubleshooting, test documentation, or analysis. Demonstrates basic scripting or automation experience, such as Python or shell scripting. Project management skills . Gantt c hart t imeline and c ritical p ath c alculations, r isk a ssessment experience , s oftware a gile e xperience as a scrum lead Has led technical triaging of issues based on level of effort, frequency, and severity Understands process for developing software requirements All listed requirements are considered essential functions of the position. Reasonable accommodations may be provided to enable qualified individuals to perform these functions. Responsibilities may change based on business needs. The estimated base salary range for the Software Test Engineer 2 role based in the United States of America is: $103,000 - $154,600. Should the level or location of the role change during the hiring process, the applicable base pay range may be updated accordingly. The range reflects long‑term growth in the role; therefore, most candidates are hired between the minimum and middle of the range. Placement depends on experience, skills, location, and internal equity. Additionally, all employees are eligible for one of our variable cash programs (bonus or commission) and eligible roles may receive equity as part of the compensation package. We offer a wide range of benefits as innovative as our work, including access to genomics sequencing, family planning, health/dental/vision, retirement benefits, and paid time off. We are a company deeply rooted in belonging, promoting an inclusive environment where employees feel valued and empowered to contribute to our mission. Built on a strong foundation, Illumina has always prioritized openness, collaboration, and seeking alternative perspectives to propel innovation in genomics. We are proud to confirm a zero-net gap in pay, regardless of gender, ethnicity, or race. cold_email.subject: Interest in Software Test Engineer 2 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Illumina Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Software Test Engineer 2 opportunity with Illumina at Illumina.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Scientist 1
jobs.description: What if the work you did every day could impact the lives of people you know? Or all of humanity? At Illumina, we are expanding access to genomic technology to realize health equity for billions of people around the world. Our efforts enable life-changing discoveries that are transforming human health through the early detection and diagnosis of diseases and new treatment options for patients. Working at Illumina means being part of something bigger than yourself. Every person, in every role, has the opportunity to make a difference. Surrounded by extraordinary people, inspiring leaders, and world changing projects, you will do more and become more than you ever thought possible. Position Responsibilities: Executes planned experiments/analysis of moderate to advanced complexity within immediate team and performs routine chemical and biochemical testing; uses insights to help troubleshoot problems Contributes ideas for meeting project goals and invention disclosures Assembles data for analysis using accepted methods and distills key conclusions while keeping an organized laboratory notebook and implementing protocols Provides supporting data to Project Lead on risks in area of responsibility Understands internal customers and collaborators and their needs and expectations May train internal customers in areas of expertise Listed responsibilities are an essential, but not exhaustive list, of the usual duties associated with the position. Changes to individual responsibilities may occur due to business needs. Position Requirements: Possesses a university level understanding of the scientific principles and laboratory experience (equivalent to Bachelor’s degree); working towards mastery of relevant subject matter Able to draw sound conclusions from general experiment data sets Can interpret results to form conclusions and suggest next steps with guidance from other scientists Uses advanced analytical instrumentation independently to collect data (examples include workstation equipment, Illumina instruments, third party analytical instrumentation, etc.) Basic understanding of statistical significance, replicates, controls Communicate with colleagues and supervisors effectively through email, presentations, written reports or in meetings to support decision-making All listed requirements are deemed as essential functions to this position; however, business conditions may require reasonable accommodations for additional task and responsibilities. Preferred Experience/Education/Skills: Typically requires a Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 0-2 years of related experience; or equivalent work experience. The estimated base salary range for the Scientist 1 role based in the United States of America is: $62,900 - $94,300. Should the level or location of the role change during the hiring process, the applicable base pay range may be updated accordingly. The range reflects long‑term growth in the role; therefore, most candidates are hired between the minimum and middle of the range. Placement depends on experience, skills, location, and internal equity. Additionally, all employees are eligible for one of our variable cash programs (bonus or commission) and eligible roles may receive equity as part of the compensation package. We offer a wide range of benefits as innovative as our work, including access to genomics sequencing, family planning, health/dental/vision, retirement benefits, and paid time off. We are a company deeply rooted in belonging, promoting an inclusive environment where employees feel valued and empowered to contribute to our mission. Built on a strong foundation, Illumina has always prioritized openness, collaboration, and seeking alternative perspectives to propel innovation in genomics. We are proud to confirm a zero-net gap in pay, regardless of gender, ethnicity, or race. We also have several Employee Resource Groups (ERG) that deliver career development experiences, increase cultural awareness, and offer opportunities to engage in social responsibility. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer committed to providing employment opportunity regardless of sex, race, creed, color, gender, religion, marital status, domestic partner status, age, national origin or ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, sexual orientation, pregnancy, military or veteran status, citizenship status, and genetic information. Illumina conducts background checks on applicants for whom a conditional offer of employment has been made. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with applicable local, state, and federal laws. Background check results may potentially result in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment. The background check process and any decisions made as a result shall be made in accordance with all applicable local, state, and federal laws. Illumina prohibits the use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in the application and interview process. If you require accommodation to complete the application or interview process, please contact accommodations@illumina.com. To learn more, visit: https://www.dol.gov/ofccp/regs/compliance/posters/pdf/eeopost.pdf. The position will be posted until a final candidate is selected or the requisition has a sufficient number of qualified applicants. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

cold_email.subject: Interest in Scientist 1 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Illumina Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Scientist 1 opportunity with Illumina at Illumina.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: QC Scientist I
jobs.description: Use Your Power for Purpose Every day, Pfizer’s unwavering commitment to quality ensures the delivery of safe and effective products to patients. Our science and risk-based compliant quality culture is both flexible and innovative, always putting the patient first. Whether you are involved in development, maintenance, compliance, or research analysis, your contribution directly impacts patients. ROLE SUMMARY The Quality Control Microbiology group is seeking a highly motivated candidate to be part of the facility utility and raw material testing group. This candidate will be responsible for performing bioburden and endotoxin testing on water samples and raw material samples, and occasionally process samples. This role also involves total organic carbon (TOC) testing, conductivity, and EM/water/clean steam sample collection. This individual will also be responsible for data review, reconciliation, SOP revision, document authoring, and other business value added work as needed. ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES • Perform bioburden, endotoxin, conductivity and TOC assays • Collect EM/water samples (monitoring) and associated testing, • Ensure all aspects of testing are performed per GMP and SOPs • Review of GMP data, reports, procedures. • Author reports and/or SOP revisions as needed. • Attend QCM at meetings and huddles Here Is What You Need (Minimum Requirements) Applicant must have a bachelor's degree with 0+ years of experience; ORan associate's degree with 4 years of experience; OR a high schooldiploma (or equivalent) and 6 years of relevant experience Knowledge and practical application of relevant techniques – classic microbiology techniques as well as rapid microbial techniques, desired. Knowledge of GMP compliance requirements for Quality Control Laboratories Experience with LWLIMS, QTS and PDOCs is a plus. Bonus Points If You Have (Preferred Requirements) A deep understanding of analytical chemistry testing and experience in defending laboratory practices during regulatory audits Solid grasp of aseptic techniques Strong problem-solving skills Ability to work independently and as part of a team Ability to ask for help and escalate issues as needed Ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously Experience using common AI tools, including generative technologies such as ChatGPT or Microsoft Copilot, to support problem solving and enhance productivity. Demonstrated curiosity for exploring how these tools can improve outcomes and understanding of responsible AI practices, including risk management and ethical use OTHER JOB DETAILS Last Date to Apply for Job: 11/9/26 Work Location Assignment: On Premise The annual base salary for this position ranges from $60,200.00 to $100,400.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 7.5% of the base salary. We offer comprehensive and generous benefits and programs to help our colleagues lead healthy lives and to support each of life’s moments. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage. Learn more at Pfizer Candidate Site – U.S. Benefits | (uscandidates.mypfizerbenefits.com). Pfizer compensation structures and benefit packages are aligned based on the location of hire. The United States salary range provided does not apply to Tampa, FL or any location outside of the United States. Relocation assistance may be available based on business needs and/or eligibility. Candidates must be authorized to be employed in the U.S. by any employer. U.S. work visa sponsorship (such as TN, O-1, H-1B, etc.) is not available for this role now or in the future. cold_email.subject: Interest in QC Scientist I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Pfizer Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the QC Scientist I opportunity with Pfizer at Pfizer.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Behavioral Health Technician (Mental Health) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Argon Agency Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Behavioral Health Technician (Mental Health) opportunity with Argon Agency at Argon Agency.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Manager of Data Analysis for Lab Production Support, Extended-Hours Support (ExHS)
jobs.description: Important: This position will work in one of the following three Extended-Hours Support (ExHS) shift teams: 1. Weekend Shift Team 1a. Rotation 1: Sunday to Thursday (9AM–5PM), Friday and Saturday off 1b. Rotation 2: Tuesday to Saturday (9AM–5PM), Sunday and Monday off 2. Early-Morning Shift Team 2a. Rotation 1: Monday to Friday (4AM–12PM Pacific Time), Saturday and Sunday off 2b. Rotation 2: Tuesday to Saturday (4AM–12PM Pacific Time), Sunday and Monday off 3. Late-Evening Shift Team 3a. Rotation 1: Monday to Friday (3PM–11PM Pacific Time), Saturday and Sunday off 3b. Rotation 2: Sunday to Thursday (3PM–11PM Pacific Time), Friday and Saturday off Important notes: During hiring, candidates will select and commit to one shift team (Weekend, Early-Morning, or Late-Evening). Once hired and onboarded, the team member will work exclusively within that shift team. ExHS team members rotate quarterly (every three months) between their team's two rotations. There are no rotations between shift teams. This is an exciting opportunity in our Data Science Production Engineering (DSPE) department at Natera (a global leader in precision medicine and genomics testing), to lead a team providing key data analytics services for our lab production operations. As a Manager of Data Analysis for Lab Production Support, you will work in one of the above three DSPE Extended-Hours Support (ExHS) shift teams, during the specified rotation hours. You will have the opportunity to apply innovative data analytics solutions, directly support the most cutting-edge medical diagnostics and genomics applications, and make real & immediate impact to patients and healthcare providers, by ensuring the specific ExHS shift team's timely and accurate data analytics support to production teams, e.g., product management team, lab operations teams, lab director teams, and genetic counselor teams. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: Leadership Lead and mentor the specific ExHS shift team, fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, and collaboration. Measure, report, and continuously improve team operational effectiveness. Define and track team objectives, ensuring alignment with broader organizational goals. Provide career growth opportunities, feedback, and performance assessments for team members. Encourage individual contributors (ICs) to pitch ideas for process improvements and innovations. Operational Excellence Ensure timely and accurate resolution of production escalations data analysis tickets. Train and coach team members on new technologies, procedures, and guidelines/best practices. Enforce operating procedures for compliance, quality, and efficiency. Manage and improve tracking systems for workload, capacity, and ticket SLAs. Communication and Collaboration Represent the Extended-Hours Support (ExHS) teams in stakeholder meetings. Proactively manage stakeholder expectations. Establish regular stakeholder reporting mechanisms. Translate complex analytical results into actionable recommendations for cross-functional partners. Effectively and correctly escalate issues encountered to other DSPE teams. Process Improvement and Innovation Identify opportunities for automation and process enhancements to streamline operations. Identify and escalate risks such as data model changes that impact project timelines or ticket TAT. Collaborate with the overall DSPE team to develop new and improve existing support solutions. QUALIFICATIONS: Master's degree in a related field (e.g., Statistics, Data Science, Computer Science). Minimum 5 years of working experience in a highly regulated environment, e.g., CLIA and/or FDA compliant settings. Minimum 5 years of hands-on experience in data analysis and/or statistical modeling in data production, data engineering, data analytics, analytics production support roles. Minimum 2 years in a team management role. Knowledge of regulatory requirements, such as HIPAA and FDA guidelines. Working knowledge of the business processes and requirements of diagnostic laboratories. Proven track record in managing production escalations, data workflows, and team operations. Experience with healthcare data, and clinical terminology is a plus. Functional understanding of next-gen sequencing workflows. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: Proficient in data analysis and statistical techniques. Proficient in Python and SQL development. Working knowledge of Snowflake platform technologies. Strong SQL skills for querying and retrieving data from complex data sources in a structured format. Strong understanding of various statistical concepts (parametric & non-parametric distributions, hypothesis testing, probability, regression). Proficient in aggregating data, preparing, cleaning data, and data mining using SQL and Python. Familiarity with machine learning techniques and their practical applications in real-world datasets. Strong leadership and team management skills. Excellent problem-solving and critical-thinking abilities. Good documentation practices and coding style. Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present technical findings to both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience using version control systems such as GitHub or GitLab for managing code and collaboration. Attention to detail and a commitment to data accuracy. Ability to work collaboratively in a cross-functional team environment. Strong integrity. The pay range is listed and actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. This may differ in other locations due to cost of labor considerations. Remote USA $140,000 — $175,000 USD OUR OPPORTUNITY Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives. The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management. WHAT WE OFFER Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program! For more information, visit www.natera.com . Natera is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace environment, and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives. Inclusive collaboration benefits our employees, our community and our patients, and is critical to our mission of changing the management of disease worldwide. All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply, and will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, age, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with applicable laws. If you are based in California, we encourage you to read this important information for California residents. Link: https://www.natera.com/notice-of-data-collection-california-residents/ Please be advised that Natera will reach out to candidates with a @ natera.com email domain ONLY. Email communications from all other domain names are not from Natera or its employees and are fraudulent. Natera does not request interviews via text messages and does not ask for personal information until a candidate has engaged with the company and has spoken to a recruiter and the hiring team. Natera takes cyber crimes seriously, and will collaborate with law enforcement authorities to prosecute any related cyber crimes. For more information: - BBB announcement on job scams - FBI Cyber Crime resource page

This position is based in South San Francisco, on site . Key Responsibilities Experimental Execution: Routinely perform onsite lab-based LC-MS workflow methods to acquire high-quality mass spectrometry biomarker data supporting target biology evaluation, drug discovery and development. Automation: Use liquid handling automation to execute automated sample preparation workflows, including protein precipitation, liquid-liquid and solid-phase extraction, and chemical derivatization. Prepare and execute global and targeted metabolomics and lipidomics protocols across diverse biological specimens, including biofluids, tissues, and cells. Data & AI Workflows: Execute mass spectrometry data processing and statistical analysis leveraging in-house AI/ML workflows and commercial software tools to scale analysis and reporting. Quality & Insight: Oversee rigorous bioanalytical quality control using common industry practices and critical analytical reasoning. cold_email.subject: Interest in Scientist II — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Genentech / Roche Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Scientist II opportunity with Genentech / Roche at Genentech / Roche.

I am especially interested in the group's effort to integrate multi-omic and clinical data with AI for biomarker and therapeutic discovery. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in bioinformatics, pipeline development, and an LLM-assisted competency-mapping project has made me especially interested in rigorous, interpretable AI for biomedical data.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

The intern will contribute to oncology discovery research using in vitro assays, flow cytometry, mammalian tissue culture, and animal tissue processing and analysis. Through hands-on laboratory experience and collaboration with scientists, the intern will build practical knowledge of oncology biology, immuno-oncology, drug discovery and translational research. jobs.description: Bold thinkers, breakthrough makers: Join a team of curious minds who challenge the status quo, create what’s next in science and technology, and have the freedom to turn daring ideas into real breakthroughs. The Opportunity The Center for Advanced Light Microscopy and Electron Microscopy (CALM-EM), housed within our Department of Research Pathology, is seeking an experienced and dedicated Scientist 3, Microscopy Specialist to join our centralized microscopy hub. In this role, you will deliver world-class technical expertise in optical microscopy and advanced quantitative image analysis to propel scientific discovery and drug development initiatives across Genentech Research and Early Development (gRED). You will partner directly with project teams across diverse therapeutic areas—providing end-to-end guidance spanning experimental design, modality selection, sample preparation, and downstream computational image analysis. Provide high-level technical consultation and experimental design across advanced imaging modalities, including confocal, live-cell imaging, organoids/complex in vitro models, tissue clearing, light sheet microscopy, and high-content screening (HCS) assays. Collaborate cross-functionally with CALM-EM team members and gRED research scientists to design, optimize, and execute tailored imaging assays that address critical drug discovery questions. Lead user onboarding and hands-on technical training on advanced light microscopy instrumentation, serving as a primary technical resource across the broader scientific community. Develop, implement, and maintain robust digital image analysis workflows and computational pipelines using scientific software to extract meaningful quantitative metrics from complex imaging datasets. Manage, maintain, and troubleshoot advanced microscope hardware platforms independently and in partnership with external service vendors. Prepare quantitative imaging data and multi-dimensional visualizations for presentation in high-impact scientific publications, patent applications, and project team reviews. Balance and prioritize multiple concurrent research projects in a dynamic, fast-paced discovery research environment. Who you are You hold Ph.D. in a scientific discipline utilizing advanced optical microscopy as a primary research methodology with 3+ years of dedicated, hands-on microscopy core or shared resource experience will also be considered. Masters level candidates with 5+ years relevant experience may be considered. Demonstrate a proven track record of teaching, mentoring, and onboarding users across advanced light microscopy hardware platforms and associated acquisition software. Bring hands-on working knowledge of advanced microscopy instrumentation, such as laser scanning confocal, spinning disk confocal, light sheet, or high-content imaging systems. Possess practical experience developing and applying quantitative digital image analysis workflows using platforms such as FIJI/ImageJ, Imaris, CellPose, or related computational tools. Exhibit strong interpersonal and communication skills with a proven history of collaborative, team-oriented problem solving across diverse scientific teams. Display exceptional time management, prioritization, and organizational skills with an established ability to rapidly adapt to and adopt emerging imaging platforms and methodologies. Preferred Direct prior experience operating within an academic or industry microscopy core facility or serving as the lead imaging technical specialist for a multidisciplinary research department. Specialized expertise in multi-modal imaging workflows (e.g., correlative optical and electron microscopy, combined live-cell and high-content imaging,). Experience with automated high-content screening hardware and software (e.g., ImageXpress Micro, IncuCyte, MetaXpress, InCarta). Advanced scripting and automation skills for image analysis workflows Practical familiarity with 3D imaging techniques including complex in vitro models, NAMs or tissue clearing methodologies and 3D volumetric light sheet imaging acquisitions. Location This is a lab-based role at our South San Francisco, CA campus. Onsite presence is required. Relocation benefits are available for this job posting. When a signed project slips, the fastest fix is often commercial: change who pays for what, who controls what, and what happens when a date is missed. This team renegotiates signed deals to get projects back on track and then makes sure what was agreed actually happens. You will be second chair on every one of those negotiations, working directly with the team lead, and we expect you to be able to run a site on your own within six to nine months. What you will do Run the issues list on live renegotiations and keep parallel papers conformed (term sheets with more than one counterparty, amendments, side letters, schedules), catching the differences before the other side does. Turn first drafts of term sheets, amendments and formal notices with in house and outside counsel. Write the internal approval memo and collect sign offs from Finance, Legal, Construction, Power and Operations. Hold the day to day channel with the developer and its counsel on deliverables, lists and dates, and escalate commercial points and misses. Visit the sites. Sit with developer and landlord management (not only the operations team) to see what is going wrong and what is going right, and turn what our construction leads are seeing into contract positions. Own version control, the notice calendar and the claims register. Help onboard two senior contract specialists on the team. You may be a good fit if you Have carried complex commercial agreements from term sheet to signature as the person holding the issues list, in real estate, energy, infrastructure, construction or project finance. Have held your ground with counterparties in challenging situations day after day without losing the facts or the relationship. Write short memos a busy executive can approve from. Have amended, restructured or worked out a project that was already in trouble. Know their way around the lender consents and financing documents that sit behind a lease. Already use AI tools to compare documents, draft and track. We can teach Data center vocabulary (commissioning levels, power feeds, ready for service conditions). Our form documents and internal approval systems. Logistics Full time. Compensation: [to be set] Regular travel to project sites in the US. Not site based. Travel 30% of the time. Annual Salary: $1 — $2 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. cold_email.subject: Interest in Patient Engagement Marketing Manager (Oncology Marketing) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Patient Engagement Marketing Manager (Oncology Marketing) opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.description: About the Team OpenAI is building the infrastructure foundation for the next generation of AI. The Data Center Engineering team defines the strategy, reference architectures, technical requirements, and delivery standards for the large-scale data centers that support OpenAI research, products, and infrastructure partners. As a Data Center Controls Engineer, you will program, configure, integrate, and commission the controls systems that support high-density AI data centers. You will work hands-on with mechanical or electrical controls, partnering with mechanical, electrical, IT/networking, security, commissioning, operations, and external delivery teams. About the Role We are seeking hands-on, early-career controls engineers with practical experience in building management systems (BMS) and mechanical controls, or electrical power monitoring systems (EPMS) and electrical controls. This role focuses on implementing and commissioning control systems, including PLCs, field devices, instrumentation, and sequences of operation, rather than owning OT/IT network or cybersecurity architecture. The ideal candidate has day-to-day experience programming and commissioning controls, ideally with a controls systems integrator. We welcome depth in either BMS/mechanical or EPMS/electrical controls; expertise in both is not required. You will work with experienced engineers and delivery partners to turn design requirements into reliable, tested systems. Key Responsibilities - Program and configure PLCs and control systems for mechanical/BMS or electrical/EPMS applications in AI data center campuses. - Implement and test sequences of operation, control logic, alarms, and interlocks against approved functional requirements. - Review and maintain controls documentation, including control diagrams, I/O and point lists, instrumentation details, sequences of operation, and commissioning records. - Integrate field devices, sensors, instrumentation, equipment controllers, and supervisory systems; validate point mapping, communications, and data quality. - Maintain control programs, configuration backups, version history, change records, and rollback procedures to support safe commissioning and operations. - Partner with mechanical, electrical, IT/networking, cybersecurity, and operations teams to resolve integration issues and implement approved OT connectivity and security requirements. - Configure and troubleshoot relevant industrial communications, such as BACnet/IP, BACnet MS/TP, Modbus TCP/RTU, OPC UA, or IEC 61850, according to the system and controls discipline. - Work directly with controls integrators, equipment vendors, contractors, and commissioning teams to resolve programming, installation, and functional performance issues. - Execute and document factory and site acceptance testing, point-to-point checks, sequence verification, and integrated systems testing; troubleshoot control logic, instrumentation, alarms, and device communication failures. Qualifications - Practical hands-on experience programming, configuring, integrating, or commissioning control systems in data centers, industrial automation, buildings, or other critical infrastructure environments. - Working knowledge of PLC programming and control logic, with the ability to implement and troubleshoot sequences of operation. - Experience in either BMS/mechanical controls or EPMS/electrical controls, with an understanding of the equipment and operating sequences in that discipline. - Experience configuring field devices and instrumentation, validating I/O and point mapping, and diagnosing control system behavior. - Working knowledge of relevant industrial communication protocols and basic OT networking needed to connect and troubleshoot control systems. - Ability to read control diagrams, equipment documentation, I/O lists, and functional specifications, and keep implementation records accurate. - Hands-on experience with functional testing, commissioning, and systematic troubleshooting using trends, alarms, logs, and field observations. - Ability to work closely with integrators, vendors, construction teams, and operations, communicate issues clearly, and follow safe work and change-control practices. - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Controls or Automation Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience. Preferred Skills - Experience at a controls systems integrator, with regular responsibility for programming, configuration, field integration, and commissioning. - Experience delivering BMS/mechanical or EPMS/electrical controls for data centers or other mission-critical facilities. - Familiarity with supervisory controls, HMI/SCADA configuration, telemetry, and historian integrations. - Familiarity with OT cybersecurity practices and working with networking or security specialists to implement approved access and connectivity requirements. - Experience with scripting, APIs, or automation tools that improve controls testing, integration, documentation, or troubleshooting. jobs.title: Pharmaceutical Development Technician, Clinical Supply Planning & Operations
jobs.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. The following positions will require the employees to work with chemical, radiological, or biological agents that may be hazardous to health if mishandled (including Agents which may potentially affect reproduction or the fetus). Employees will be required to follow all safety procedures and use personal protective clothing/Equipment where specified. Inquires for further information should be directed to the hiring manager. Permanent Position – Pharmaceutical Development Technician, Clinical Supply Planning & Operations – 25 – CSO Shift: 7 AM - 3:30 PM EST Site: NBR Bldg # 105/109 (excluded) Rate: $42.04 / hour JOB FUNCTION: The goal of Pharmaceutical Development within Research & Development (R&D) is to develop new drug candidates and the processes to manufacture them into commercial realities. This is achieved by designing and conducting a variety of experimental studies using the latest scientific methods and state of the art equipment and instrumentation. The development process is very dynamic with performed in both laboratory and process scale-up facilities. Scientific rigor, timeliness and compliance with all cGLP/GMP and federal/state/local regulations are a necessity. In order for the development process to be successful, there must be excellent collaboration between the professional and union staffs. Often, the professional staff will need to take a hands-on approach during the course of an experiment as necessary based on sound scientific judgment. Involvement of the union staff in the various experimental studies and other processes is determined by the professional staff on a case by case basis because of the non-routine, dynamic nature of the development process. Daily assignments will be based on demonstrated technical competence of the individual technician and the demands of the process. Priorities will be set based on the needs of the R&D business. Both written procedures and verbal instructions by a supervisor will be executed with strict attention to safety and quality. Accurate and timely execution and documentation of activities and results are a requirement. Strict adherence to cGLP/GMP, federal, state and local regulations is required. Collaborative work with other employees is a necessity to achieve departmental and company goals. JOB FUNCTION – CLINICAL SUPPLY OPERATIONS INTEGRATED SUPPLY CHAIN Assignments within Integrated Supply Chain include, but are not limited to the following: Weigh, dispense and accurately label bulk drug substances, ingredients, dosage forms, packaging components, and all materials needed to support clinical programs and product development Withdraw samples from material containers, transfer materials between buildings and within buildings by means of hand trucks or fork lifts Setup, clean and operate all areas and equipment required in the weighing and dispensing process Record data as per cGLP and cGMP regulations in both paper and computer formats, per established procedures Maintain the warehouse, dispensaries and other operations areas in neat and tidy conditions Perform the receipt, reconciliation and put-away of inbound materials Pack and ship both regular and temperature controlled, domestic as well as international shipments JOB FUNCTION – CLINICAL SUPPLY OPERATIONS REGIONAL LOGISTICS Assignments within Regional Logistics include, but are not limited to the following: Perform the physical and system pick of finished clinical supplies for domestic and international shipments, ensuring the accuracy of the items picked to the container level Pack finished clinical supplies for domestic and international shipments Pack temperature controlled shipments to maintain temperature range specified for the product, according to the provided cold chain packing guidelines Perform inventory/cycle counts of finished supplies within New Brunswick Perform drug re-labeling activities and domestic and international shipment labeling EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS : Two year Associate Degree in Science related to Pharmaceutical Development or Business related to Operations/Supply Chain/Logistics or equivalent. Proficiency in the use of computer programs/systems is essential. Technicians must maintain their skills and knowledge current with advances in the field of Pharmaceutical Development. Incumbents may attend internal or external training courses as approved by management. Training will be implemented to ensure PDT employees receive relevant training to facilitate the performance of their job responsibilities. Testing after training specific to an area will be an ongoing requirement. Interactive training modules will be used for training on specific competencies. If testing is not passed, the interactive learning and testing will be repeated. A pass/repeat summary of all testing on each module will be kept to assess the performance of the module. WORKING CONDITIONS : The position will require the employee to work with chemical, radiological and biological agents that may be hazardous to health if mishandled (including agents which may potentially affect development of the fetus). Assignments will be executed in laboratory, warehouse and process scale-up facilities interchangeably. The employee will be required to follow all safety procedures and use personal protective clothing/equipment as provided by the company where specified. Disagreeable conditions including odors, heat, noise etc. may be experienced. The following positions will require the employees to work with chemical, radiological, or biological agents that may be hazardous to health if mishandled (including Agents which may potentially affect reproduction or the fetus). Employees will be required to follow all safety procedures and use personal protective clothing/Equipment where specified. Inquires for further information should be directed to the hiring manager. We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway. Compensation Overview: The pay range for this position at commencement of employment is expected to be $42.04 per hour. The Pharmaceutical Development Technician, Clinical Supply Planning & Operations position will be covered by the collective bargaining agreement between Bristol Myers Squibb and the United Steel, Paper and Forestry, Rubber, Manufacturing, Energy, Allied Industrial and Service Workers International Union (USW) and its Local 4-438. For more on benefits, please visit https://careers.bms.com/life-at-bms/ . cold_email.subject: Interest in Pharmaceutical Development Technician, Clinical Supply Planning & Operations — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Bristol Myers Squibb Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Pharmaceutical Development Technician, Clinical Supply Planning & Operations opportunity with Bristol Myers Squibb at Bristol Myers Squibb.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
